facts.fact: Broadcast stations must offer candidates their best rates during the 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general election, a protection the page says CTV platforms do not have.
facts.value: 45 days before a primary; 60 days before a general election
facts.quote: During the 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general election, broadcast stations must offer candidates their best rates.

facts.fact: For candidate ads, the FEC disclaimer must read "Paid for by [candidate committee name]."
facts.quote: For candidate ads, the disclaimer must read: "Paid for by [candidate committee name]."

facts.fact: Federal candidates' spoken approval must come from the candidate, either on-screen or as a voiceover with the candidate's image visible for at least four seconds.
facts.quote: The spoken approval must come from the candidate directly, either on-screen or as a voiceover with the candidate's image visible for at least four seconds.

facts.fact: PAC and third-party ads must state that the ad is "not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee" when applicable.
facts.value: not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
facts.quote: PAC and third-party ads need to identify the paying organization and state that the ad is "not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee" (when applicable).

facts.fact: Roku's creative review process for political ads takes 3-5 business days, according to the page's summary of Roku's requirements as of early 2026.
facts.quote: Creative review process (allow 3-5 business days)

facts.fact: Hulu, Roku, Peacock, Tubi, and Pluto TV are described as not broadcast licensees, so FCC political advertising provisions do not extend to them.
facts.quote: CTV platforms like Hulu, Roku, Peacock, Tubi, and Pluto TV are not broadcast licensees.

facts.fact: Netflix launched its ad-supported tier in 2022 and initially did not accept political advertising, according to the page, which advises checking current policy.
facts.quote: Netflix** launched its ad-supported tier in 2022 and initially did not accept political advertising

facts.fact: Apple TV+ does not currently accept advertising of any kind, according to the page.
facts.quote: Apple TV+** does not currently accept advertising of any kind

facts.fact: California's DISCLOSE Act requires that the top three funders of an ad appear in the disclaimer for ads paid for by committees.
facts.quote: The state's DISCLOSE Act mandates that the top three funders of an ad appear in the disclaimer for ads paid for by committees.

facts.fact: New Jersey updated its election law in 2023 to require disclaimers on digital political advertising, including streaming video.
facts.quote: New Jersey updated its election law in 2023 to require disclaimers on digital political advertising, including streaming video.

facts.fact: New Jersey's law requires the 'paid for by' disclosure to be 'clear and conspicuous' in the ad itself.
facts.quote: The law requires the "paid for by" disclosure to be "clear and conspicuous" in the ad itself.

facts.fact: Texas SB 1571 prohibits publishing deceptive AI-generated videos in the 30 days before an election and applies broadly to digital distribution.
facts.quote: Prohibits the publication of deceptive AI-generated videos in the 30 days before an election. Applies broadly to digital distribution.

facts.fact: California AB 2655 requires disclosure when political ads contain AI-generated or significantly altered content and applies to all distribution channels, including streaming.
facts.quote: Requires disclosure when political ads contain AI-generated or significantly altered content. Applies to all distribution channels, including streaming.

facts.fact: The page says platform verification for political CTV advertisers typically takes 3-10 business days, and can take longer during peak political season.
facts.quote: This process typically takes 3-10 business days but can take longer during peak political season.

facts.fact: The page recommends building at least 5-7 business days of lead time into a media plan for creative approvals on CTV platforms.
facts.quote: Build at least 5-7 business days of lead time into your media plan for creative approvals.

facts.fact: For a 30-second federal political CTV spot, the 'stand by your ad' requirement needs at least four seconds of candidate visibility.
facts.quote: The "stand by your ad" requirement for federal candidates needs at least four seconds of candidate visibility.

facts.fact: The page advises planning 4-6 seconds of disclaimer screen time in a 30-second CTV spot.
facts.quote: 4-6 seconds of disclaimer screen time.

facts.fact: The page recommends setting a monthly check during campaign season to review new political advertising legislation or regulatory guidance.
facts.quote: Set a monthly check during campaign season to review any new legislation or regulatory guidance.

facts.fact: Maryland passed a law requiring platforms to maintain a public file of political ad purchases, similar to the FCC's broadcast political file.
facts.quote: Maryland** passed a law requiring platforms to maintain a public file of political ad purchases, similar to the FCC's broadcast political file.

facts.fact: Washington requires disclosure when political ads use 'synthetic media' that depicts a real person.
facts.quote: Requires disclosure when political ads use "synthetic media" that depicts a real person.

facts.fact: Retain CTV political ad compliance records for at least two years after the election cycle.
facts.quote: Retain these records for at least two years after the election cycle.

facts.fact: Platform verification should start 60-90 days before a planned CTV political ad launch date.
facts.quote: Starting the process 60-90 days before your planned launch date gives you time to resolve any documentation issues without losing ad inventory.

facts.fact: Plan for at least 5-7 business days of lead time for CTV platform creative review of political ads.
facts.quote: Plan for at least 5-7 business days of lead time for creative review, and longer during peak election season when review queues are backed up.

facts.fact: The number of states with AI disclosure requirements for political ads doubled between 2023 and 2025, according to the page.
facts.quote: The number of states with AI disclosure requirements for political ads doubled between 2023 and 2025, and more states are expected to act before the 2026 midterms.

facts.fact: The FCC issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking in 2024 exploring whether CTV platforms should maintain public files of political ad purchases; no final rule has been adopted.
facts.quote: In 2024, the Commission issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking exploring whether CTV platforms should be required to maintain public files of political ad purchases

facts.fact: Honest Ads Act and similar bills had not passed as of early 2026.

facts.fact: For federal candidates, FEC requires a 'Paid for by [committee name]' disclosure and an 'I approve this message' statement on every ad regardless of platform.
facts.quote: For federal candidates, the FEC requires a "Paid for by [committee name]" disclosure and the candidate's "I approve this message" statement on every ad, regardless of platform.

facts.quote: CTV platforms can accept or reject political advertising at their discretion.
